summary:
Tamil Nadu is India's most protective sub-national regime for trans visitors. It was the first state to introduce a transgender welfare policy (1995), maintains a dedicated Transgender Welfare Board (as the Third Gender Welfare Board since 15 April 2008) within the Social Welfare & Women Empowerment Department, and adopted a comprehensive State Policy for Transgender Persons in 2025. On 4 August 2025, the Madras High Court (WP 7284 of 2021) expressly commended the policy as "a victory for transgender and intersex persons after their long struggle" — active judicial confirmation of executive protection is rare and meaningful for a visitor's institutional recourse. Tamil Nadu was the only state recording a Transgender Persons Act case in 2020 (1 of 1 nationally) and logged 7 of the 11 national cases in 2023 — its courts are demonstrably being used.

Against the national 0.43, Tamil Nadu sits +0.10. The state has a functioning (by comparison) policy apparatus, court validation, and the Thirunangai/Thirunambi administrative categories embedded in governance. Compared to Kerala (0.50), Tamil Nadu adds the explicit court commendation and longer institutional history; compared to Punjab (0.35), which saw a religious authority veto trans public assembly, Tamil Nadu's state machinery actively protects it. A complicating signal exists — Hindu transgender devotees in Madurai announced a fast in December 2025 over temple lamp-lighting decisions — but this reflects trans people as political actors in state governance, not state suppression of them.

sources.summary: Official Tamil Nadu Transgender Welfare Board portal (Social Welfare & Women Empowerment Department): documents the Thirunangai/Thirunambi categories, membership ID cards and the "Tamil Nadu State Policy for Transgender persons - 2025"; records Tamil Nadu as the first Indian state with a transgender welfare policy (free surgery in government hospitals, housing, citizenship documents, scholarships, income-generation programmes) and trans recruitment into police, health and welfare services through 2020.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (never cached); the underlying document is the Madras High Court order of 4 August 2025 (WP 7284 of 2021) noting with approval that the state brought into effect the Tamil Nadu State Policy for Transgender Persons 2025, calling it "a victory for transgender and intersex persons after their long struggle" and expressly commending the government.

queerbeat data report (30 Jan 2026): per the NCRB, the Transgender Persons Act recorded only 20 cases nationwide 2019-2023 - 1 in Tamil Nadu (2020); 7 in 2021 (2 each in Assam and Kerala, 3 in West Bengal); 1 in Tamil Nadu (2022); 11 in 2023 (7 Tamil Nadu, 4 Kerala), none from north and central India; it attributes the scarcity to police registration bias, against survey data showing 27.2% physical and 22.3% sexual violence prevalence (2025 Transgender Health study, n=4,964).

Press Information Bureau reply in the Rajya Sabha (8 Dec 2021, Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar): 12 states/UTs have constituted Transgender Welfare Boards under section 10(1) of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Rules, 2020 - Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Chandigarh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

localsOnly: The board's resident-facing machinery — membership ID cards, free surgery, housing, scholarships, state employment quotas — benefits trans residents of Tamil Nadu; what a visitor encounters is the institutional climate these signal.
